Should you Build your LatAm engineering team, or Buy an existing team?

A recent example of buying is when Capacity, a US AI customer support platform, acquired Chattigo, a Chilean AI CX company, for around $60M. Chattigo had hit $10M ARR on just $2M raised. Capacity got a LatAm team, Spanish-language AI tuned for the market, and WhatsApp Business integration in one move.

It's a great case study in "buying" a team through acquisition instead of building one through recruiting. But acquisitions are risky, expensive, and depend entirely on the right target being for sale at the right time.

I think there's a third option that gets overlooked: Build, Operate, Transfer. You get a dedicated LatAm team built to your standards from day one, run by a partner who handles the legal and operational complexity, with the option to fully own it once it's performing. Best of both worlds, without the M&A risk.

This is a service we offer at AgilityFeat, and so in this week's LatAm AI Engineering newsletter, I dove into the tradeoffs between Building and Buying. 

I say, why not both? What do you say?

As AI Agents become more capable, evaluating them requires a different mindset from testing traditional software. 
Traditional applications tend to follow predefined, largely deterministic rules. 𝐀𝐈 𝐀𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬, 𝐡𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫, 𝐦𝐚𝐤𝐞 𝐝𝐲𝐧𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐜 𝐝𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐟𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐨𝐰 𝐝𝐢𝐟𝐟𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐨𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐩𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐬 𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧 𝐰𝐡𝐞𝐧 𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐯𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐬𝐚𝐦𝐞 𝐭𝐚𝐬𝐤.
That means evaluation is not only about asking “Did it work?” -  it is also about understanding: 𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐝𝐢𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐮𝐥𝐭?
 - Did it follow the expected workflow and required steps?
 - Did it avoid actions it was not supposed to take?
 - Was the final outcome correct and useful?
 - How much time did the process take?
 - What was the cost of the agent run?
 
During our fifth 𝐀𝐈 𝐓𝐚𝐥𝐤𝐬 session, Claudiu-Emilian Voinescu introduced 𝐋𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐟𝐮𝐬𝐞, an open-source LLM engineering platform that helps teams bring more visibility into agent-based applications through 𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐢𝐧𝐠, 𝐨𝐛𝐬𝐞𝐫𝐯𝐚𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐞𝐯𝐚𝐥𝐮𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧.

Using a practical 𝐍𝐓𝐓 𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐮𝐦𝐞-𝐛𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐮𝐬𝐞 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐞, we explored how Langfuse can help inspect an agent's execution flow, LLM interactions and tool usage, while also evaluating both 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐟𝐥𝐨𝐰 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 and 𝐟𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐬.

And evaluation is not only for AI engineers.
 - 𝐒𝐨𝐟𝐭𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐞 & 𝐀𝐈 𝐄𝐧𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐞𝐫𝐬 can use it for tracing, automated evaluations and identifying regressions.
 - 𝐓𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐬, 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭 𝐌𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐃𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐢𝐧 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐭𝐬 can contribute by defining quality criteria, creating test scenarios, reviewing agent behavior and providing human evaluation.
